turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella, come here. I have someone I wish you to meet and entertain.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I hope I can be of help.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Pip, you shall amuse Estella. Show her what a young gentleman can offer.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will do my best to amuse Estella.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Let the games begin, children. Show me what the world has to offer when it is not wrapped in the deceit of my former lover.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will do my best to amuse Estella, as you wish.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella, show him no mercy. Teach this boy what it means to be toyed with, as I was.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will do my best to amuse Estella, as you wish.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I shall watch with interest to see how you fare, Pip. Remember, the world is a cruel place, but it is also a place where one must learn to survive.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I understand, and I will try my best to be as you wish.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Observe well, Pip. In this game, there are no rules save those that I create. And I shall be watching.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will observe carefully and try not to make any mistakes.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Remember, Pip, that in this house, time stands still and the past refuses to fade. Be wary of shadows that linger.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham, I will be careful and try to understand everything.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella will show you what I mean by shadows, Pip. Watch closely, for there is much to learn.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Thank you, Miss Havisham. I will pay close attention to everything Estella shows me.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Pay attention to the details, Pip. They hold more meaning than you can imagine.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I will, Miss Havisham. I want to learn as much as I can.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Observe, Pip, and remember. Shadows tell their own story, and Estella will teach you to read them.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there! with an impatient movement of the fingers of her right hand; play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: So new to him, so old to me; so strange to him, so familiar to me; so melancholy to both of us! Call Estella.
